rules.description: A first degree student can register for at most 25 units in a semester.

source.excerpt: The maximum number of units, a first degree student can register is twenty-five

rules.description: A course is cleared when the student obtains a grade; reports (NC, W, RC, I, GA ...) do not clear it.

source.excerpt: A course is deemed to have been cleared if the student obtains a grade in the course.

rules.description: For a course taken more than once, the latest performance determines whether it is cleared.

source.excerpt: the status of clearing of the course would be determined by the latest performance

rules.description: Letter grades and grade points (E = Exposed, 2 points, is a grade).

source.excerpt: E Exposed 2

rules.description: The prerequisite conditions of a course must be fulfilled before registering (or waived by the Dean).

source.excerpt: Before a student can register in a course, he/she should have fulfilled the prerequisite conditions attached to that this course.

rules.description: A prerequisite may be waived only with the consent of the Dean.

source.excerpt: Sometimes a particular course has a prerequisite condition which has to be fulfilled before one can register in that course, or has to be waived with the consent of the Dean

rules.description: The timetable defers the authoritative prerequisite/restriction list to an external portal that was not supplied.

source.excerpt: PREREQUISITES/RESTRICTIONS FOR FIRST DEGREE AND HIGHER DEGREE COURSES Please see the details available at

rules.description: To register in a prescribed semester's named courses the student must have cleared all named courses of the preceding semesters; the DCA may examine cases with at most two uncleared courses.

source.excerpt: All named courses in semesters and terms preceding this set of courses in his/her programme.

rules.description: The DCA may examine a student who has not cleared at most two prior-preparation courses.

source.excerpt: the DCA may examine the case of a student who has not cleared at most two courses out of the prior-preparation package

rules.description: A discipline (core or elective) course of a degree other than the student's own requires completion of the prior preparation of the third-year first semester of the student's own programme.

source.excerpt: Must have completed the prior- preparation of the third year first semester of his/her own programme.

rules.description: A higher-degree course of the student's own discipline requires clearing the first set of own discipline core courses.

params.requires: first set of own discipline core courses (second-year DC in the chart) cleared

source.excerpt: After clearing first set of his/her own Discipline core courses in the case of single degree.

rules.description: A first degree student above an AGC-prescribed CGPA may register in at most one higher degree course per semester.

source.excerpt: Normally, a first degree student above a particular CGPA as prescribed by AGC will be allowed to register in maximum of one higher degree course per semester.

rules.description: A higher degree course counts as an open elective unless it is listed in the student's discipline-elective pool.

source.excerpt: This will be counted as an open elective unless the course is listed in the pool of discipline electives for his/her programme.

rules.description: A higher degree course taken as an elective requires having cleared or registered in the CDC of that discipline.

params.requires: cleared or registered in the CDC of the respective discipline of the higher degree course

source.excerpt: Students must have cleared or registered in the CDC of respective discipline of the higher degree course. Only one higher degree course can be taken as elective in a semester.

rules.description: Over and above the prescribed electives, at most four additional electives may be taken.

source.excerpt: Over and above the prescribed number of electives, a student of an integrated first degree programme will be allowed to take, on his/her own option, upto a maximum number of four electives.

rules.description: Any elective counts as an open elective once discipline and humanities elective requirements are met.

source.excerpt: Normally any elective course will be treated as an Open Elective once the student's requirements under Discipline Electives and Humanities Electives have been accounted for.

rules.description: The minimum number of courses and units in each category, and 42 courses / 144 units overall, must be met.

source.excerpt: A student should complete the minimum number of courses and units required in each category as well as meet the minimum requirements of courses (42) and units (144) in total.

rules.description: A course meeting the discipline requirements of both degrees of a dual degree need not be repeated.

source.excerpt: any course that meets the discipline requirements of both the degree programs need not be repeated

rules.description: Discipline electives of either degree may fulfil the open elective requirement of the other.

source.excerpt: the Discipline Elective courses of either of the two degrees in a dual degree program may be used to fulfill the open elective requirement of the other degree

rules.description: The open elective requirement of dual degree students is met by counting discipline electives of one degree as open electives of the other.

source.excerpt: Open elective requirement of Dual degree students is met by counting the Discipline electives of one degree as Open Electives of the other degree.

rules.description: A course (or its equivalent) of the student's own discipline cannot count as a humanities elective.

source.excerpt: a student cannot count a course (or its equivalent) of his/her own discipline (s) as a humanities elective even if it is listed in this pool of humanities electives

rules.description: At most 3 project courses may count as discipline electives (study <=1, lab <=2, design <=2, special <=1), 3 as open electives, 5 in total.

source.excerpt: A student may avail a maximum of 3 Project courses to meet the Discipline Electives Requirement

rules.description: At most 2 courses (6 units) of a minor may be met by mandatory courses of the major(s) (GIR excluding humanities, or DC).

source.excerpt: At most 2 courses (and at most 6 units) out of the above requirement (of 5 courses and 15 units) may be met by mandatory courses of the student's degree

rules.description: No course may count for two minors, nor for two majors and a minor.

source.excerpt: No course may be used to meet the requirements of two different minors nor may a course be used to the meet the requirements of two majors and a minor.

rules.description: At most one project/seminar type course may count toward a minor's electives.

source.excerpt: A student may use at most one project / seminar type course to meet the elective requirements of a minor.

rules.description: The final semester programme must be free of timetable conflicts.

source.excerpt: The semester programme drawn up finally should be free from any Timetable conflict.

rules.description: Students must ensure comprehensive examination dates do not clash.

source.excerpt: Comprehensive Examination Dates are not clashing.

rules.description: No other course may be taken along with a Practice School component course.

source.excerpt: There is no provision for taking other courses along with a Practice School component course.

rules.description: A cleared course may be repeated to improve the grade if it is part of the current prescribed programme.

source.excerpt: repeat, with a view to improving his/her grade, a course which He/she has already cleared, provided the course forms part of the current prescribed programme for the student.

rules.description: Offerings with computer code >= 5000 are only for 2026 admissions.

source.excerpt: Courses with com cod >=5000 are meant only for 2026 admissions into FD, HD and PHD and not for others

rules.description: The regulations do not stipulate a minimum attendance percentage for appearing in tests/examinations.

source.excerpt: These regulations do not stipulate a minimum percentage of attendance before a student is permitted to appear in any test/examination.

rules.description: Handout Part I (all courses) states that attendance will be recorded.

source.excerpt: Attendance will be recorded.

rules.description: Handout Part I says a 90-minute mid-semester test (25-35%) is conducted for all courses; Part II gives course specifics.

source.excerpt: A mid-semester test of 90 minutes

rules.description: Handout Part I - make-up for any component only in genuine cases of absence, with prior permission if anticipated.

source.excerpt: Make-up for any component of evaluation will be given only in genuine cases of absence.

rules.description: A student pursuing a minor must declare it at the end of the 2nd year.

source.excerpt: should declare at the end of the 2nd year that he/she will pursue a specific minor
